title: Establish pricing governance: approval flow, pricebook refresh, and discount guardrails
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Sales and AE teams have been granting ad-hoc discounts and custom terms for Dedicated and Private deployments without a central approval process. This leads to revenue leakage, inconsistent pricebook usage, and delayed legal/security questionnaire reviews.

Goal: Define and implement an internal pricing governance process that covers (1) an approval workflow for non-standard pricing and contract concessions, (2) a maintained canonical pricebook for Hosted/Dedicated/Private SKUs and add-ons, and (3) discounting guidelines / guardrails with escalation thresholds. The policy must integrate with Salesforce/GTM workflows and surface approvals in our contract tracker.

Deliverables: canonical pricebook spreadsheet (Drive), an approval playbook (Confluence) for Sales/Finance/Legal/Security sign-offs, a lightweight automation spec for Slack/GitHub/Confluence notifications, and updated sales enablement content.

Scope: enterprise deals, Dedicated capacity commitments, Private on-prem licenses, and add-on observability/compliance packages. Excludes micro freemium credits and standard hosted API list pricing changes (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: Published canonical pricebook (Drive link) with SKU-level list prices and suggested quantity bands for Dedicated/Private
A documented approval matrix in Confluence mapping discount thresholds to required approvers (Sales Manager, Finance, Legal, Security for >30% or >$200k ARR concessions)
Playbook for routing security questionnaire (SSQ) items that require Legal/Security review with SLA targets (3 business days triage, 10 business days completion)
Template emails and Slack workflows for routing approvals; at least one automation PR created in github.com/redwood-inference/internal-ops
Training session held with GTM (recording and slide deck uploaded) and update to deal desk SOPs
